description:
Work that is needed starts when it is needed. Today a producer nobody has run yet starts only when the ready queue is empty: next_ready_job (src/compiler2/drive.rs) pops queued work first and only then calls demand_root_frontier_seeds, demand_activation_frontier_analyses and demand_blocked_wait_producers. A wait on a fact whose producer never ran creates no wake, and a gate redirect (demand_producer_if_needed) queues the gate's producer but leaves no subscription behind, so the comment there ("the gate's own wake reaches this job the ordinary way once it lands") is false for a job that never ran. A climbing recursive cycle keeps the queue non-empty, so every pending chain advances one link per drain and starves until the widening budget ends the climb.

Consequence: how much work a compile does, and the program it produces, depend on what else happens to be queued.

Evidence (base 5ea6a5830, top of stack #258; probes in scratch xxd10/a and xxd10/b):
- Ladder starvation, xxd10/b/s/s3.fz (9 lines, val/arr/item JSON-like parser calling Map.put): with the Map.put extern not yet expanded, ExpandFunctionSource(fz_map_put_int) runs and wakes nobody; DefineFunction waits 702 jobs while arr/item climbs val 16 times and widens it to any. A variant (s1) flips which binary is unlucky. json_roundtrip at base: object_value blocks on FunctionContract(Map.put/3) from job 1073; DeriveFunctionContract runs at 1779, after the array climb widened val.
- Order changes the compiled program: json_roundtrip canon(BackendProgram) differs between base and fz-xxd.10 revision 3 (base Json.val/1 = any, 220 executable keys vs 212). With a probe that runs demand_blocked_wait_producers before every pop (xxd10/b/eager_probe.patch), both produce byte-identical canon on json, s1 and s3; base json 3216 -> 2571 jobs, val ladder 17 widened -> 7 rungs; s3 on rev3 843 -> 179.
- Activation frontier one depth per drain, xxd10/a/p1.fz (16 lines, closure_capture_requirement_projection shrunk): a minted activation whose caller does not wait on it (return from contract/@spec) sits in activation_frontier until a drain; the chain wrap-lambda -> mailbox -> Kernel.* -> fz_op_mul_* -> arithmetic_result -> arithmetic_error -> panic -> fz_panic takes 10 drains instead of 1 (base pays this once, for fz_op_mul_ff).
- Original case: fixtures2/behavior/return_tuple_ladder.fz on fz-afu.10. dbg/1's activations block on FunctionContract and Recursive(fz_dbg_value/1) at step 142; their producers run at steps 194/197 behind ~36 ladder analyses; all 17 dbg/1 activations run 3 times where 2 suffice. Order-caused single runs in fz-afu.10 pins (authorized 2026-09-26): enum_predicate_search AnalyzeActivation 551 -> 552; enum_take_drop_split Recursive wakes 47 -> 49; 00420 activation frontier 265 -> 266.

Direction (paper first, page ../fz-afu.13.html before any build): recording a wait, a gate redirect, or minting an activation starts the producer at that moment (or subscribes the waiter so the producer's landing wakes it); the drain only settles quiescent waits. What goes away: the drain-time ignition sweeps over root_frontier/activation_frontier and blocked waits, and with them the subject of fz-afu.9 (stall sweep counting).

Signal: runs per subject and wake causes in work_graph.applied; canon(BackendProgram) equality across schedules.
Close when: the tuple ladder's dbg/1 activations analyze at most twice each (34 in all); s3 and s1 climb val at most 4 rungs on both base orderings with identical canon; p1's callee chain is analysed without a drain per depth; json_roundtrip canon is the same as the eager probe's; no pin rises without owner approval.
title: Needed work starts when it is needed, not when the queue drains
